claims.text: Single-phase ZrB2 requires synthesis or sintering temperatures above 2300 °C.
Single-phase ZrB2 has strong Zr–B and B–B bonds.
Lower-temperature-processed ZrB2 has limited oxidation resistance.
Lower-temperature-processed ZrB2 has limited resistance to liquid plating-metal corrosion.
A minor silicon or silicon-containing addition to ZrB2 will produce a transient liquid phase during sintering near 1700 °C.
The transient liquid phase will aid densification of the silicon-doped ZrB2.
The silicon addition lowers the densification temperature of ZrB2 through liquid-phase sintering.
During cooling or subsequent high-temperature exposure, the added silicon will oxidize to SiO2.
The resulting SiO2 will form a continuous layer along grain boundaries and exposed surfaces.
The silica-based surface scale will passivate ZrB2 against high-temperature oxidation.
The silica-based scale will prevent or reduce corrosion by liquid plating metals.
Silicon-doped ZrB2 sintered near 1700 °C will attain densification comparable to conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2.
Silicon-doped ZrB2 sintered near 1700 °C will attain mechanical integrity comparable to conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2.
Silicon-doped ZrB2 will have statistically significantly better high-temperature oxidation resistance than both conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 and lower-temperature undoped ZrB2.
Silicon-doped ZrB2 will have statistically significantly better liquid-metal corrosion durability than both conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 and lower-temperature undoped ZrB2.
The proposed material is applicable in oxidizing service around or above 1100 °C.
The proposed material is applicable to prolonged service in reactive liquid plating baths.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires only comparable densification and mechanical integrity, whereas the falsification rule requires statistically significant improvements in densification and mechanical strength over both controls. The falsification criterion is therefore stronger than the stated prediction.
The design says all samples use identical processing routes except for silicon addition, but the high-temperature control is processed above 2300 °C while the other groups are processed near 1700 °C.
